answer: Cross-epoch reputation delta hashing. Each identity commits a hash of its behaviour vector per epoch; the next epoch reveals it, and the system scores divergence between predicted and observed conduct. An identity whose trajectory stays consistent across a voyage of many epochs accrues low divergence; fresh clones inherit none. To pass, an attacker must sustain coherent behaviour for many epochs across every clone, paying full operating and sync cost per identity. Divergence above threshold at any summit of the audit resets history. Consistency unlocks a grove of trust multipliers,
